newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse shares edge up, market in lull.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse shares edge up, market in lull.

text.p: Selected key shares at the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) rose marginally on speculative buying by courageous investors willing to make a gamble in an election year, brokers said.

They said the NSE 20-share index gained 10.72 points to close at 3427.83. Turnover was posted at 17.8 million shillings traded on 719,949 shares compared to 32.9 million shillings on 747,083 shares on Friday.
A senior broker at a leading brokerage company said there was an increasing trend among investors to buy shares in "strong" companies after they traded ex-all (without bonus and dividend).
"Their prices tend to recover and what's happening is that these shares are scarce in the market," another broker said.
Nation Printers & Publishers traded at 120 from 118 while Marshalls (E.A) closed at 80.50 from 71.50.
Kenya Commercial Bank traded at 102 unchanged -- a price level brokers say is sustained purely by foreign demand.
Meantime Brooke Bond gained to 125 from 123 while Kakuzi gained three shillings to close at 108. Rea Vipingo closed at 9.05 from 9.
"A lot of investors I'm talking to now do not want make any serious buys' before the elections. They're saying to wait," one broker said.
Kenya's parliamentary and presidential elections must be held before the end of the year, the electoral commission says.
Kenya Power & Lighting shed five shillings to close at 165 while Total Kenya was unchanged at 65.
Barclays Bank eased to 111 from 112 while Uchumi Supermarket closed at 40.25 from 41.
The Central Bank of Kenya floating rate treasury bond traded nine million shillings at 105.4635 percent from 104.7588 percent.
